title: Coulomb, mAh, Ah: Charge Units and Battery Capacity
h1: Charge units — coulomb, mAh and ampere-hour
description: 1 A·h = 3600 C. A 3000 mAh phone battery is 10 800 C. Confusing energy (Wh) with charge (Ah) is the number one battery-spec error.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: Charge (C or Ah) is not energy (Wh). Multiply Ah by voltage to get Wh. Ignore voltage and lithium and lead-acid look interchangeable — they are not.
body: Charge and energy are related but distinct. Charge is quantity of electrons; energy is charge times voltage. Battery specs frequently muddle them, and equivalent-sized packs from different chemistries deliver wildly different runtimes.

> 1 A·h = 3600 C
> 1 mA·h = 3.6 C
> Energy (W·h) = charge (A·h) × voltage (V)

Coulomb: electrochemistry, capacitor sizing, semiconductor doping. mAh, Ah: batteries, small-signal current integration, plating time. C-rate: discharge/charge current expressed as multiples of Ah capacity (a 3 Ah pack at 2C draws 6 A).
Two power banks: 20 000 mAh at 3.7 V vs 6000 mAh at 12 V. Charge: 20 vs 6 Ah. Energy: 74 vs 72 Wh — essentially identical. Buyers who compare mAh alone miss the voltage rescaling.
Ah is charge. Wh is energy. Multiply by voltage to compare.

faqs.a: Yes — 1 F = 1 C/V. A 1 F cap charged to 1 V stores 1 C of charge.
Charge out ÷ charge in per cycle. Lithium is 99.9%+, lead-acid 85–90%.
